t.1.117.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having performed the concluding ablution for Pāṇḍu, the great seers, who were like gods, those ascetics, then came together and held counsel.
t.1.117.2: Having abandoned both his kingdom and his realm, that great-souled one, rich in austerities, came to this place to practise austerities and took refuge with the ascetics.
t.1.117.3: King Pāṇḍu, having entrusted to you here, as a sacred deposit, his newborn sons and his wife, has gone from this world to heaven.
t.1.117.5: The noble-minded Siddhas set their minds on going, in order to hand over the Pāṇḍavas to Bhīṣma and to Dhṛtarāṣṭra as well.
t.1.117.6: At that very moment all the ascetics set out, taking them with them: Pāṇḍu's wife, his sons, and his body as well.
t.1.117.4: Having consulted one another, they, devoted to the welfare of all beings, placed the sons of Pāṇḍu before them and set out for the city named after the elephant.
t.1.117.7: Though she had formerly lived in comfort, she, ever devoted to her sons, having set out upon the long road, deemed it short.
t.1.117.9: Then, hearing of that arrival of the sages, thousands of Cāraṇas, wonder arose among the men in Nāgapura.
t.1.117.10: When the sun had risen but a moment before, all the townsfolk, placing dharma foremost, went out with their wives to see the ascetics.
t.1.117.8: Before long she reached Kurujāṅgala, and the glorious lady arrived at the Vardhamāna gate of the city.
t.1.117.11: Throngs of women and throngs of warriors, mounted on throngs of carriages, went forth together with the brahmins, and so too did the wives of the brahmins.
t.1.117.12: Likewise there was a great mingling of the throngs of vaiśyas and śūdras. No one showed envy; all were of righteous mind.
t.1.117.15: The heirs of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, a hundred in number, led by Duryodhana and adorned with splendid ornaments, came forth.
t.1.117.13: Likewise Bhīṣma, the son of Śāṃtanu, Somadatta and Bāhlika, the royal sage whose eyes are wisdom, and the steward Vidura himself.
t.1.117.14: Queen Satyavatī, the illustrious Kausalyā, and Gāndhārī, surrounded by the wives of the king, came forth.
t.1.117.16: Having saluted all those hosts of great seers by bowing their heads, all the Kauravyas, together with their family priests, sat down near them.
t.1.117.17: In the same way, all the people of the city and the countryside too, having greeted them with their heads to the ground and bowed down, sat down near them.
t.1.117.19: Then the eldest among them, a great seer wearing matted locks and an antelope skin, rose up and, having understood the mind of the great seers, spoke these words.
t.1.117.20: He who was the heir of the Kauravas, the king of men named Pāṇḍu, who, renouncing the enjoyments of pleasure, went from here to Śataśṛṅga
t.1.117.18: Then, perceiving that throng of people to be silent, as it were, on every side, Bhīṣma offered the kingdom and the realm to the great seers.
t.1.117.21: Of him, who was steadfast in the vow of celibacy, this son Yudhiṣṭhira was born through a divine cause, directly from Dharma himself.
t.1.117.22: Likewise Mātariśvan, the Wind, gave to that great-souled king this son, the best of the strong, named Bhīma, of mighty strength.
t.1.117.23: This one, of true valor, was born to Kuntī from Puruhūta; his fame will surpass all great archers.
t.1.117.24: And those two great archers, the best of the Kurus, whom Mādrī bore from the two Aśvins, here they stand as well, these two tigers among men.
t.1.117.25: This ancestral lineage has been raised up once more by the glorious Pāṇḍu, ever devoted to dharma, while he was living a life of dwelling in the forest.
t.1.117.26: As Pāṇḍu continually beheld the birth of his sons, their growth, and their Vedic studies, his joy grew ever greater.
t.1.117.28: Knowing that he had come to the funeral pyre and been offered as an oblation into the mouth of Vaiśvānara, Mādrī entered the fire, giving up her own life.
t.1.117.27: Abiding in the conduct of the good and having obtained sons, Pāṇḍu has gone to the world of the ancestors, having passed away on the seventeenth day.
t.1.117.29: She, devoted to her husband, has gone together with him to the world of her lord. Let whatever rites are due for her and for him now be performed without delay.
t.1.117.31: And when the funeral rites have been completed, let the greatly renowned Pāṇḍu, knower of all dharma and upholder of the Kuru lineage, receive the ancestral offering.
t.1.117.32: Having spoken thus to all the Kurus, all the Cāraṇas, together with the Guhyakas, vanished in an instant while the Kurus looked on.
t.1.117.30: These are the two bodies of those two, and these are their excellent sons. Let these scorchers of foes, together with their mother, be favoured with the proper rites.
t.1.117.33: Seeing the host of seers and Siddhas, which looked like a city of the Gandharvas, vanish again right there, they were filled with the greatest astonishment.
